diagnostics.message: The literal `res://../assets/aircraft/ugly-stik-60/appearance.json` does not exist on disk (no file and no directory). Nothing here proves it is loaded, so this is a warning — but a `res://` string in a script is almost always a path that is about to be opened, and the load will return null.
diagnostics.suggested_fix: Create `res://../assets/aircraft/ugly-stik-60/appearance.json`, fix the path, or — if the file is produced at runtime — write it through `FileAccess.open(…, FileAccess.WRITE)` / `ResourceSaver.save()`, which the linter recognises and stops reporting. `# lint:ignore res_path` on the line silences it for good.

diagnostics.message: `:=` from `get_node()` / `get_node_or_null()` compiles, but infers the bare type `Node`, so every later member access on the variable is unchecked and only fails at runtime. In a project that raises `unsafe_property_access` / `unsafe_method_access` it becomes a parse error as well.
diagnostics.suggested_fix: Annotate with the node's real class: `var timer: Timer = get_node("Timer")`. See references/gdscript_conventions.md.
